To view a copy of this license, visit http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . Adult-onset Still’s disease (AOSD) is a multi-systemic inflammatory disorder of unknown etiology. To date, no single diagnostic test is available for AOSD. Herein, we investigated the pathogenic role of microRNAs in AOSD. MicroRNA profiles in plasma from AOSD patients and healthy controls were analyzed by microarray analysis, followed by quantitative reverse transcription PCR validation. The biological functions of microRNAs were evaluated using in vitro cell-based assay. Among the differentially expressed microRNAs, microRNA-134 (miR-134) expression was positively correlated with AOSD activity scores and significantly decreased after effective treatment. An increased miR-134 level is significantly associated with the activation of Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3). The reporter assay identified IL-18 binding protein (IL-18BP) as the target of miR-134. A negative correlation between miR-134 expression and IL-18BP mRNA levels were detected in peripheral blood cells following TLR3 ligand treatment. Lower plasma IL-18BP levels and higher IL-18 levels were also observed in active AOSD patients who had higher miR-134 expression than inactive patients. Upregulation of circulating miR-134 was associated with elevated IL-18 levels by targeting IL-18BP in AOSD patients and was positively correlated with disease activity, suggesting its involvement in AOSD pathogenesis. MiR-134 may be a novel activity indicator or potential prognostic biomarker in AOSD. issue-copyright-statement © The Author(s) 2017 Introduction MicroRNAs (MiRNAs) are short non-coding RNAs composed of approximately 20 to 24 nucleotides that mediate messenger (m)RNA cleavage, translational repression, or mRNA destabilization 1 – 3 , and currently more than 2,000 human miRNAs are registered (miRBase Release 20.0) 4 . MiRNAs have recently been identified as immune regulators that post-transcriptionally repress target mRNAs expression 5 , and they have diverse functions in immune cell development, particularly the development of Th17 cells 2 , 3 . The deregulated expression of miRNAs has been observed in different pathological conditions, including rheumatic and inflammatory diseases 5 – 8 . Recent studies have revealed that miRNAs are present in a remarkably stable form in plasma and are thought to have potential as clinical biomarkers or therapeutic targets 9 – 11 . Adult-onset Still’s disease (AOSD) is a rare inflammatory disease of unknown etiology that usually affects young adults, which is characterized by fever, rash, arthritis, variable multisystemic involvement, and an increase of acute phase reactants 12 , 13 . To date, determining predictive factors of outcome and to drawing guidelines for patient management remains difficult 14 , 15 . Previous studies, including ours, have demonstrated elevated levels of proinflammatory cytokines including interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, IL-18, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and type 1 T helper (Th1)- or Th17-derived cytokines in AOSD patients 16 – 21 . Moreover, an increase of spontaneous and IL-18-induced apoptosis plays an important role in AOSD pathogenesis 22 . Curtale et al . also demonstrated that miR-146a was involved in T-cell activation and could modulate activation-induced apoptosis 23 . These observations led us to hypothesize that miRNAs may play an important role in AOSD pathogenesis. No data are available, however, concerning the expression of circulating miRNAs in AOSD patients. In the present study, we investigated differential miRNA expression in plasma from AOSD patients compared with healthy controls using microarray profiling followed by quantitative reverse transcription PCR (QRT-PCR) validation. The associations of candidate miRNAs expression with clinical activity scores or disease outcome were examined in AOSD patients. We used a bioinformatics tool to search for potential targets of candidate miRNAs and subsequently used 3′ untranslated region (UTR) reporter assay for validation. Additionally, we explored the biologic roles of candidate miRNAs in AOSD pathogenesis using an in vitro cell-based functional assay.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the pathogenic role of microRNAs in Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD), identifying circulating microRNA-134 (miR-134) as a key biomarker. MiR-134 expression was found to be significantly upregulated in active AOSD patients, positively correlated with disease activity scores, and decreased after effective treatment. Mechanistically, miR-134 is induced by Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) activation and contributes to AOSD pathogenesis by downregulating IL-18 binding protein (IL-18BP) expression, which in turn elevates free Interleukin-18 (IL-18) levels. The study proposes miR-134 as a potential diagnostic and activity biomarker for AOSD, and suggests TLR3 or miR-134 as potential therapeutic targets.

treatment_details.therapy_type: The study primarily focused on the investigation of Adult-onset Still's Disease (AOSD) pathogenesis and associated biomarkers, specifically microRNAs, and their molecular mechanisms. It also involved observing the effects of pharmacological treatments in AOSD patients and conducting experimental interventions.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Patient treatment involved corticosteroids, NSAIDs, conventional synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, sulfasalazine), and in some cases, an IL-6 receptor inhibitor (tocilizumab). Specific patient numbers were provided for csDMARDs (e.g., 10 patients for methotrexate). Experimentally, various Toll-like receptor (TLR) ligands were used for stimulation (e.g., poly (I:C) at 50 µg/ml for 24h, inducing a 3.81 ± 0.09 fold increase in miR-134 in PBMCs). MicroRNA mimics and inhibitors were transfected at 50 nM overnight, and a TLR3 inhibitor (bafilomycin A1, 5 nM for 2h) and TLR3 RNAi lentivirus (MOI of 5) were also used. The study primarily describes observations of disease states and experimental conditions rather than specific therapeutic dose-response comparisons.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma (circulating), Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMCs), U937 human monocytic cells, THP-1 human monocytic cells, miR-134 over-expressing cells

measured_effect.direction_of_change: higher in active disease, lower after effective treatment/remission, up-regulated by TLR3 activation
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression was positively correlated with AOSD activity scores and significantly decreased after effective treatment/clinical remission (mean ± SEM, 5.30 ± 2.19 vs. 0.84 ± 0.56, P < 0.05). Significantly higher levels in active AOSD plasma (128.60 ± 47.72 fold) compared to healthy controls (5.25 ± 2.26 fold) (P < 0.01), and active AOSD (mean 6.4-fold) compared to inactive AOSD (mean 2.4-fold, P < 0.01) and controls (mean 0.3-fold, P < 0.001). Upregulated in PBMCs from active AOSD (147.70 ± 28.25 fold) compared to healthy controls (0.53 ± 0.13 fold) (P < 0.0001) and inactive AOSD (1.91 ± 0.44 fold) (P < 0.0001). Higher in active/inactive AOSD plasma/PBMCs compared to SLE patients (P < 0.01 / P < 0.0001). Significantly increased by TLR3 ligand poly (I:C) in PBMCs (3.81 ± 0.09 fold, P < 0.01) and THP-1 cells (1.92 ± 0.11 fold, P < 0.01). Higher expression observed in AOSD patients with systemic inflammatory pattern (96.04 ± 35.74 fold) vs. chronic articular pattern (3.04 ± 0.36 fold) (P = 0.143, not statistically significant).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Mediates mRNA cleavage, translational repression, or mRNA destabilization; acts as an immune regulator; involved in AOSD pathogenesis by targeting IL-18BP and being associated with elevated IL-18 levels; involved in innate immunity; regulation of gene expression.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Adult-onset Still’s disease (AOSD) activity, effective treatment/clinical remission, activation of Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3), distinguishing AOSD from Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), systemic inflammatory pattern of AOSD, TLR3 ligand stimulation, miR-134 over-expression/mimic/inhibitor transfection.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Novel activity indicator or potential prognostic biomarker in AOSD; indicates disease activity and involvement in pathogenesis; specific biomarker for distinguishing AOSD from SLE; linked to TLR3 ligand stimulation, suggesting involvement of innate immunity in AOSD pathogenesis; indicates clinical remission in AOSD; associated with a systemic inflammatory pattern in AOSD.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma, Peripheral blood cells (for mRNA), THP-1 cells supernatant, miR-134 over-expressing cells, serum
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein level, mRNA level, Gene Transcript

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: A negative correlation between miR-134 expression and IL-18BP mRNA levels was detected in peripheral blood cells following TLR3 ligand treatment. Lower plasma IL-18BP levels were observed in active AOSD patients who had higher miR-134 expression. Significantly lower protein levels (mean, 38.6 pg/ml) in miR-134 over-expressing THP-1 cells compared to miR-134 inhibitor-expressing cells (67.2 pg/ml, P < 0.01) and mimic control-expressing cells (52.7 pg/ml, P < 0.05) or non-transfection (50.4 pg/ml, P < 0.05). Significantly decreased IL-18BP mRNA following miR-134 upregulation associated with TLR3 ligand stimulation. Lower plasma levels in active AOSD patients (mean, 4441.6 pg/ml) compared to inactive AOSD patients (5572.5 pg/ml, P = 0.155, not statistically significant). Low rate of expression in miR-134 over-expressing cells; reduced plasma levels in active AOSD patients with high miR-134; previous studies showed lower serum levels in active AOSD vs. inactive AOSD.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Target of miR-134; binds IL-18; its reduction by miR-134 is associated with elevated IL-18 levels; intrinsic inhibitor of IL-18; modulates inflammation by binding to IL-18, neutralizing its proinflammatory activity; inhibits IL-18-mediated NF-κB activation and proinflammatory cytokine production.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Active Adult-onset Still’s disease (AOSD), following TLR3 ligand treatment, miR-134 over-expression, miR-134 mimic- or inhibitor-expressing THP-1 cells, AOSD pathogenesis.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates AOSD activity; targeted by miR-134, contributing to the disease pathogenesis through its effect on IL-18; negative regulation by miR-134 leads to increased free IL-18, contributing to inflammation; decreased levels contribute to increased free IL-18, promoting inflammation in AOSD; potentially associated with increased disease activity; its decline contributes to enhanced free IL-18 levels; low expression may lead to insufficient binding of IL-18; contributes to elevated free IL-18 levels and AOSD pathogenesis; involved in the biologic effect of miR-134.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Plasma, U937 cells supernatant, THP-1 cells supernatant, miR-134 over-expressing cells, serum

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Higher IL-18 levels were observed in active AOSD patients who had higher miR-134 expression than inactive patients. Upregulation of circulating miR-134 was associated with elevated IL-18 levels. Markedly higher expression of IL-18 in miR-134 over-expressing U937 cells (mean, 39.7 pg/ml) compared with mimic control-expressing cells (22.7 pg/ml, P < 0.05) or non-transfection cells (22.5 pg/ml, P < 0.05). Significantly higher levels (mean, 121.3 pg/ml) in miR-134 over-expressing THP-1 cells compared with inhibitor-expressing cells (57.3 pg/ml, P < 0.01), mimic control-expressing cells (72.0 pg/ml, P < 0.01), or non-transfection (62.5 pg/ml, P < 0.01). Significantly higher levels in active AOSD patients (mean, 3844.0 pg/ml) compared to inactive AOSD patients (mean, 1863.6 pg/ml, P < 0.05) and controls (mean, 112.0 pg/ml, P < 0.001). Increased circulation of IL-18 in AOSD. Free IL-18 levels specifically elevated in AOSD.
